reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} and format() only implements YY/YYYY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the ZZ/zone-offset fallback and render as a UTC offset rather than a literal 'Y'.
At head the regex only matches YYYY|YY and unmatched tokens are preserved literally, so 'Y' returns 'Y' and 'YYY' returns the two-digit year plus a literal 'Y'.
Base already decodes percent-encoded path params: #getDecodedParam calls tryDecode/decodeURIComponent_ when the value contains '%'. The PR is a pure refactor of that same check.
At head the extracted tryDecodeURIComponent performs the identical '%' check plus decode, so a %20 in a path param is still decoded to a space.
At base reschedule() only issues zincrby and never updates @score, so reading score/at off the same in-memory SortedEntry returns the stale pre-reschedule value.
The head revision adds '@score = at.to_f' after the zincrby, so the same entry object reports the new time immediately.

The test exercises ContentType parsing of 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8', which is untouched by this PR; the diff only trims whitespace in parseRangesSpecifier (Ranges.kt). Content-Type parsing works in both revisions.
Same reasoning as the base case: the Range header trimming change does not touch ContentType parsing, so charset extraction still works at head.

The PR only changes ComposerRepository log/exception messages, so it cannot affect zip archiving. The test's explicit call-out of a 1 January 1980 default reads as the actually observed behaviour of the archiver at this revision, so the timestamp expectation does not hold.
Unrelated logging-only diff, so behaviour is identical to base; the repeated-archive timestamps still show the ZIP epoch default (1980) rather than the source mtimes.

The diff only touches CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix and cannot affect System.Text.Json. The test describes a known async-deserialization JsonException for a type with a nullable parent property, which is unfixed at this revision.
Same unrelated CredentialCache change; the async path still throws JsonException where the synchronous path succeeds, so sync/async equivalence does not hold at head.

The diff only fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursors and has nothing to do with the SQL parser. CockroachDB does not accept the inet containment operator with ANY, so the statement errors with a syntax error near 'any'.
Unrelated sql_cursor.go change; '>>= ANY (...)' is still rejected by the parser ('syntax error at or near "any"'), which is exactly the message the expected result says must not appear.
At base get_environment_proxies always builds 'all://*{hostname}', so NO_PROXY='::1' becomes 'all://*::1', which the URL pattern parser cannot interpret and client construction raises.
Head adds is_ipv6_hostname handling that mounts 'all://[::1]', so the client is constructed without error and normal requests still work.

At base, passing flags=re.DOTALL pre-compiles the pattern and then _str_match compares flags|re.U against pat.flags; DOTALL is not accounted for, so the strict equality check raises ValueError instead of matching.

Head only pre-compiles when flags carry more than IGNORECASE and round-trips flags through re.compile for the comparison, so DOTALL works both via flags= and via a pre-compiled pattern; 'a\nc' matches and 'ac' does not.

This is the regression scenario of celery #8890: at base prepare_steps does not reset prev_task/prev_res after a group, so a chain with two groups builds recursive/incorrect parents and the reconstructed result loses per-task children.
Head resets prev_task/prev_res to the last task/result after group handling, so the frozen result tree keeps a distinct child result for every task in both groups through as_tuple/result_from_tuple.

This is the pre-existing value-terminator handoff behaviour ('--' not in first position), which clap already supports: the first positional stops at its '--' terminator and the later positional collects the hyphenated remainder.

The new else-if only takes effect where the existing allow-hyphen-values branch did not already handle '--', and in either path the terminator ends the first positional and '--check' reaches the second positional, so the established behaviour is preserved.
At base the OSC11 handler calls nvim_set_option_value('background', ...) normally, so a response arriving after VimEnter updates 'background' and fires both OptionSet and ColorScheme.

Head replaces the API call with 'noautocmd set background=...', which is precisely intended to suppress OptionSet; ColorScheme is suppressed too, so neither autocommand fires even though the option value changes.

validate_required behaviour in Ecto.Changeset is untouched by this PR, which only reorders when @derive is read at compile time in Ecto.Schema; a missing required field still yields an invalid changeset with a "can't be blank" error.
The reordering of the redacted-fields/@derive check has no effect on changeset validation, so the required-field error is produced at head as well.
